races.paceDynamic: Baggot Street and Spiced Gold are the confirmed front runners who will contest the early lead in this 17-runner handicap. With two genuine pace-setters, they should establish an honest gallop from the start, potentially going hard enough to set up the race for closers. The large field and competitive pace means the leaders will come under pressure turning for home, creating opportunities for strong finishers to pick up the pieces. This pace scenario clearly favours hold-up horses and late-running types who can capitalize on the expected pace collapse.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Favours Closers
scenarios.trigger: If Baggot Street and Spiced Gold duel early and fade
scenarios.body: The two front runners will ensure a genuine pace that sets up perfectly for hold-up horses. Strong closers like Happy Henry, Wegotogether, and Jazzit can time their runs to perfection as the pace-setters weaken.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong but one prominent runner stays close enough
scenarios.body: A horse like Step Back In Time or Dinamine can track the early pace without getting involved in the battle, then strike when the leaders falter. Their proven course form gives them an edge in this scenario.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If Baggot Street breaks clear and the pace isn't as strong as expected
scenarios.body: Despite having Spiced Gold for company, Baggot Street could use his blinkers first time to dictate terms and hold on. The maiden has shown consistent form and the headgear change could provide the needed improvement.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Benefits From Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the large field creates a messy pace with multiple moves
scenarios.body: A lightly-weighted outsider like Lismacbryan or Platino Bianco could benefit from tactical positioning in a slowly-run race. The lack of early pressure would neutralize the closers' advantage and allow a different type to prevail.

watchPoints.text: Baggot Street could steal a march if the pace isn't as strong as expected despite having Spiced Gold for company
Happy Henry's strong-travelling style could be perfectly suited if the front runners duel early
Step Back In Time has excellent course form but trainer Chris Timmons is 0/1 in the last 14 days
Several runners including Dinamine, Lismacbryan and Spiced Gold are returning from lengthy absences
Multiple horses carry warnings about fading in the finish which could be crucial in a competitive handicap

races.paceDynamic: Namiid looks the only confirmed front runner and should get an uncontested lead with most others content to settle behind. Reposado and Ennoble are the main prominent runners but both have shown they can track rather than press. With a modest pace likely through the early stages, this sets up perfectly for the closers to unleash their finishing kicks in the final two furlongs. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses who can produce late acceleration over those dependent on early positioning.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Closer's Paradise
scenarios.trigger: If Namiid sets modest fractions and the field bunches up
scenarios.body: The pace collapse allows late runners like Keogie and Xerling to sweep past tired leaders. Those who showed early speed get swamped by the late charge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Escapes
scenarios.trigger: If Namiid kicks clear turning for home and the pace was too slow
scenarios.body: The leader gets first run and holds off the closers who leave their effort too late. Prominent runners like Ennoble get best of both worlds.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens mid-race and tests stamina reserves
scenarios.body: Those tracking just behind the leader like Reposado can strike at the right moment before closers get organized. Early pace becomes crucial positioning.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Maiden Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the proven performers underperform and newcomers step up
scenarios.body: Trek Home or Allirelandmaterial produce debut efforts that catch the market leaders cold. Breeding suggests they have ability to find.

watchPoints.text: Namiid breaking too fast early could set up perfect pace scenario for the closers behind
Trek Home and Allirelandmaterial for market support as their breeding suggests significant ability
Ennoble for signs of fitness after 206-day layoff, any positive move would signal readiness
Keogie and Xerling for tactical positioning, both need to be held up for maximum effect
Grande Cuvee for early keenness again, repeat of debut tactics would compromise his chances

runners_data.note: Prominent runner stepping up significantly in class, 212 days absence is worrying for 5yo mare
runners_data.comment: Two 5f wins last year, returns off career high mark and may need this after 212 days off
runners_data.spotlight: Two 5f wins last year, off 63 at Newmarket (good) in August and off 67 on her final start at the Curragh (yielding) for this rider; career high mark now and record fresh suggests she'll need this run after a 212-day absence.

runners_data.name: Nouvel Espoir
runners_data.note: Hold-up style perfectly suited to expected pace shape, won over course and distance off lower mark
runners_data.comment: C&D winner, raised 3lb for close third at Naas on latest, this is a stronger race
runners_data.spotlight: Three turf wins include one over C&D (yielding) off 5lb lower; sole win last year at Cork (5f, gd-yld) and was beaten just 0.5l off the same mark at Naas on latest (5f, good); raised 3lb for that and this is a deeper race.

runners_data.name: Cuban Grey
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with solid course form, placed efforts suggest he's competitive at this level
runners_data.comment: 4-22 on turf, has run well in defeat over C&D, remains 2lb above highest winning mark
runners_data.spotlight: Six-time winner is 4-22 on turf; last two wins have come at the Curragh but has run well in defeat over this C&D on more than one occasion; shaped well at Bellewstown on penultimate but needs to bounce back from poor Curragh run latest; 2lb above highest winning mark.

runners_data.name: Nezeeh
runners_data.note: Course and distance winner last September off similar mark, hold-up style suits likely pace scenario
runners_data.comment: Four wins last year included one over C&D off 1lb higher, badly out of form this season
runners_data.spotlight: One of two for yard; kept busy last year and four wins included one over C&D (good) in September off 77 and just 1lb higher here; subsequently won off revised mark of 84 at Bellewstown in October; badly out of form so far this year, however, and needs a revival.

runners_data.name: Eclairage
runners_data.note: Confirmed leader but 0-7 turf record is major concern despite impressive all-weather strike rate
runners_data.comment: 4-6 on AW, rated 8lb lower on turf, best turf runs on Flat tracks, may be best watched
runners_data.spotlight: Speedster has an impressive strike rate of 4-6 on the AW; last seen in October running a fine race when a 2l fourth of 14 in Dundalk Group 3 (5f); 0-7 on turf and rated 8lb lower and rider claims 7lb; best turf runs have come on flat tracks so might be best watched on seasonal return over this stiff 5f.

runners_data.name: Lethimfly
runners_data.note: Will press for early lead but limited recent form and struggles to win make him vulnerable
runners_data.comment: Had Cuban Grey behind when running well on return at Dundalk, same mark here
runners_data.spotlight: No joy since landing a 5f Bellewstown 2yo maiden (good) in 2024; only seen twice last season; fine run on reappearance at Dundalk (5f) in March when a 0.75l second (Cuban Grey 4.75l behind); same mark here and can go well if backing that up on return to turf.

races.paceDynamic: Eclairage and Lethimfly will contest the early lead, with both confirmed front-runners ensuring a genuine gallop from the start. Alfred Tennyson, Howd'yadoit and the prominent runners will track close behind the leaders through the opening two furlongs. The strong early pace will set up the race for hold-up horses to close late, with Midnight Dusk and Nouvel Espoir ideally placed to strike in the final furlong. This pace scenario clearly favours hold-up horses who can benefit from the inevitable collapse of the pace-setters.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-up horses prevail
scenarios.trigger: If Eclairage and Lethimfly duel early and weaken
scenarios.body: The strong early gallop will suit closers who can pick up the pieces as the leaders tire. Midnight Dusk and Nouvel Espoir are perfectly positioned to capitalise.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent tracker strikes
scenarios.trigger: If one prominent runner avoids the early pace battle
scenarios.body: A horse like Howd'yadoit or Alfred Tennyson can track the leaders without getting embroiled in the early speed duel. They can then kick clear when the pace-setters weaken.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-runner holds on
scenarios.trigger: If Eclairage gets an uncontested lead
scenarios.body: Without Lethimfly pressing early, Eclairage could dictate terms and prove hard to peg back despite his poor turf record. The class advantage from his Group 3 effort could tell.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Moderate pace develops
scenarios.trigger: If both leaders are restrained early
scenarios.body: A steadier gallop would favour the prominent runners who can position closer throughout. Mary Shoelaces could benefit from the reduced emphasis on a finishing kick.

watchPoints.text: Eclairage's turf form is abysmal (0-7) despite his all-weather ability - major red flag for the likely favourite
Harry's Hill returns after 217 days off which is concerning for an 8yo, despite his previous course success
Midnight Dusk sports first-time cheekpieces after his staying-on effort at Naas suggests more improvement
Alfred Tennyson represents Denis Hogan's struggling yard (1/30) but showed promise at Dundalk in March
Both Mary Shoelaces and Harry's Hill face significant fitness concerns after 200+ day absences

races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Yeats Stakes (Listed Race)

runners_data.name: Asakir
runners_data.note: Promising prominent runner who backed up debut win impressively at Leopardstown, though faces step up in class here
runners_data.comment: Leopardstown maiden win franked; big step up in trip here and faces quicker ground
runners_data.spotlight: Zarak gelding backed up a promising Curragh debut in March when made plenty of use of in beating a subsequent winner in 1m2f Leopardstown maiden last month, both those runs on softish ground; big step up in trip here and faces quicker conditions now.

runners_data.name: Limestone
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner with tongue-tie added, perfectly positioned to control this race with his proven make-all tactics
runners_data.comment: Race to suit when winning at Cork; type to progress and could improve for this longer trip
runners_data.spotlight: Progressed nicely in each of three juvenile runs, notably making all in Listowel rated race on heavy ground (1m); followed up on seasonal return when tongue-tied in 1m2f Cork conditions last month, dictating steady pace then battling well; Derby entry looks the type to keep progressing and could well improve for this longer trip.

runners_data.name: Sangreal
runners_data.note: Lightly raced prominent type making just her second start, pedigree suggests this trip will suit but needs to improve significantly
runners_data.comment: Leopardstown maiden second should improve and win races but this looks a big jump in grade
runners_data.spotlight: Camelot filly a 270,000gns yearling; half-sister to winners Roi De France (Listed-placed 1m inc AW; RPR 112) and Vaguely Royal (1m4f Flat inc AW, 100; 1m7f hurdle); dam 1m/8.5f winner (inc AW 2yo/US turf stakes; 97); promising debut run in Leopardstown fillies maiden last month when chasing home a clear winner over 1m2f; should improve and win races but this looks a big jump in grade.

runners_data.name: New Zealand
runners_data.note: Most experienced runner with Group race form, blinkers applied suggest connections want him more prominent early
runners_data.comment: Highest-rated but bit to prove after below-par seasonal return at Epsom
runners_data.spotlight: The most experienced of these, having won Curragh 2yo maiden and twice campaigned in Group company, notably fifth in Group 1 Criterium International; underwhelming seasonal debut, however, in Epsom Classic Trial last month, weakening quite tamely final furlong; blinkers now tried and upped in trip.

runners_data.name: Trojan Fighter
runners_data.note: Progressive type coming off maiden win just 8 days ago, rapid turnaround could be positive or negative for improvement curve
runners_data.comment: Impressive Ballinrobe maiden winner; Carmers completed same double for yard last year
runners_data.spotlight: Ulysses colt didn't run at two but three runs already this term, showing plenty of improvement to land Ballinrobe maiden over this trip eight days ago, making virtually all to win handsomely (good-to-yielding); yard took same route with last year's winner Carmers en route to an Ascot success so demands plenty of respect.

runners_data.name: Star Of Tara
runners_data.note: Completely outclassed hold-up runner returning from 274-day break, tactical disadvantage compounds class deficit
runners_data.comment: Beaten a long way in four maidens at two; completely out of her depth
runners_data.spotlight: Beaten a long way in four maidens at two; completely out of her depth.

races.paceDynamic: Limestone will lead from the gates with no other confirmed pace-setters, creating a sustainable tempo over this 1m5f trip. The O'Brien runner has proven front-running credentials including making all at Listowel, and faces no early pressure with Asakir, Sangreal, New Zealand and Trojan Fighter all sitting prominent but unlikely to challenge for the lead. This moderate gallop will allow Limestone to dictate terms before the field converges in the straight. This race shape clearly favours front-runners and prominent racers who can track the leader, as they'll have first run on any hold-up horses in a potentially tactical finish.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Limestone Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Limestone maintains his lead unchallenged through moderate fractions
scenarios.body: The O'Brien runner can use his proven front-running ability to kick clear in the straight before the prominent pack can mount their challenges. This sustainable pace perfectly suits his tactical profile and recent form suggests he has the class edge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pack Converges
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent runners close the gap turning for home and engage Limestone
scenarios.body: New Zealand's Group race experience and Asakir's recent Leopardstown victory give them the class to outstay Limestone in a driving finish. The moderate early pace allows these horses to use their natural speed from tracking positions.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Trojan Fighter Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Twomey's runner improves again off his recent Ballinrobe maiden win
scenarios.body: The progressive three-year-old can use his stamina-laden pedigree and current form momentum to wear down the leaders in the final furlong. His prominent style positions him perfectly to strike when the pace lifts.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If the slow pace creates a sprint finish that suits versatile types
scenarios.body: New Zealand's class and tactical speed could prove decisive if the race becomes a dash from the two-furlong pole. The Ballydoyle runner has Group-level form that would shine in a truly-run finish.

watchPoints.text: Star Of Tara is completely outclassed and returning from a 274-day layoff - avoid completely
Trojan Fighter runs just 8 days after his maiden win which could either aid fitness or hinder recovery
New Zealand needs the blinkers to help him settle better early or his Group class means little from off the pace
Limestone's tongue-tie addition suggests connections want him more aggressive early, which suits the race shape
Sangreal makes just her second career start and needs significant improvement to compete at Listed level

races.name: Royal County Handicap

runners_data.name: Madbadanddangerous
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with 34 days since last outing, trainer Noel Meade in moderate form but horse has strong recent record
runners_data.comment: Solid form as a 2yo, fine run on h'cap debut on return, in the mix again off 3lb higher
runners_data.spotlight: Close second in Tipperary maiden (7.5f, yielding) on debut; off the mark on next start in 7f Naas maiden (soft); 2l third in valuable auction series final over same C&D (soft); narrowly denied on seasonal return/handicap debut at Leopardstown latest (10.5f, gd-yld); reliable and in the mix again off 3lb higher.

runners_data.name: Manton Bay
runners_data.note: Classic hold-up performer, only 19 days since promising handicap debut at Naas where he showed renewed vigor
runners_data.comment: 1m Dundalk maiden winner, fine run on 1m h'cap debut latest, should stay this far, chance
runners_data.spotlight: Built on promising debut run at the Curragh (6f, yld-sft) to win a Dundalk maiden (1m) last November; pleasing run on handicap debut/seasonal return at Naas last month (1m, good) when beaten 0.5l; raised 2lb; should stay this far on breeding; chance.

runners_data.name: Santa Bravado
runners_data.note: Hold-up style suits the likely pace scenario, making handicap debut off a workable mark of 79
runners_data.comment: Handicap debutant, promise in maidens at 8f-1m2f, worth a market check
runners_data.spotlight: Handicap debutant; best effort a 2.75l fifth of 16 on debut at the Curragh (1m, yielding); held by Manton Bay on Dundalk running in November; mildly promising run on return over 1m2f at Naas; potential improver worth a market check.

runners_data.name: Now Maybe
runners_data.note: Another hold-up runner making handicap debut, showed promise when third at this track and distance on return
runners_data.comment: Close up behind 83 rated rival here latest, opening mark doesn't look a gift but respected
runners_data.spotlight: Handicap debutant; struggled on heavy on debut; beaten a nose over 7f at Dundalk in November; 3l third of 18 in C&D maiden on seasonal return, close up behind 83 rated rival; opening mark doesn't look a gift but very much respected.

runners_data.name: Minella Rockett
runners_data.note: Prominent early but 176 days since last run is a major concern despite Seamie Heffernan booking
runners_data.comment: Two excellent runs over 1m at Dundalk in Nov', form of latest run solid, chance if fit
runners_data.spotlight: Handicap debutant; promise in Tipperary maiden last August; proved that was no fluke with a 1l third behind Manton Bay at Dundalk (1m) in November; denied by a short head over the same C&D later that month; should stay this far on breeding and the form of his last run has worked out; chance if ready after break.

runners_data.name: Johnny Soda
runners_data.note: Prominent style with recent breakthrough win at Cork, stamina-laden pedigree suits this longer trip
runners_data.comment: Stayed on strongly to win at Cork (1m), up 5lb, go well again if handles quicker ground
runners_data.spotlight: Breakthrough win at Cork (1m, soft) on latest, outpaced before coming from the back to score by 0.5l; looked better the further he went so this longer trip should suit; this is harder but should go well again off 5lb higher if handles quicker ground (brother won on good to firm).

runners_data.name: Fallacy
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner but has shown tendency to fade in the finish, making handicap debut off lowest mark in field
runners_data.comment: Modest form in 1m AW and turf maidens, best watched up in trip unless market speaks
runners_data.spotlight: Handicap debutant; didn't show much in a trio of 1m maidens on the AW last year and on good to yielding at Cork on return; probably best watched upped in trip unless the market speaks.

races.paceDynamic: Madbadanddangerous will set a controlled pace from the front with Johnny Soda and Minella Rockett providing some early company in the opening stages. With no genuine speed horses in this field, the gallop will be steady through the first six furlongs before gradually winding up from the three-furlong pole. The hold-up horses Manton Bay, Santa Bravado, Now Maybe and Fallacy will have ample time to get organized in the rear divisions as the pace builds progressively. This sustainable tempo strongly favours the closers and hold-up performers who can produce their best work in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Closing Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the pace remains modest through halfway and quickens from the three-furlong pole
scenarios.body: The hold-up horses get the perfect setup to unleash their kicks, with Manton Bay and Santa Bravado ideally positioned to strike. The front-runners fade as the closers surge past in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Sustained Gallop Benefits
scenarios.trigger: If Madbadanddangerous maintains a stronger tempo throughout the middle stages
scenarios.body: The more prominent runners stay competitive longer, allowing Johnny Soda's stamina to tell and Minella Rockett to stay in contention. The hold-up horses still threaten but face a stiffer task.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominance
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely and becomes a crawl until very late
scenarios.body: Madbadanddangerous gets away with murder up front and proves hard to peg back despite the closing efforts. The hold-up horses leave their runs too late on such forgiving fractions.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Surprise Breakthrough
scenarios.trigger: If the favorites underperform and the pace becomes messy with false dawns
scenarios.body: Now Maybe or Santa Bravado capitalize on the chaos with perfectly-timed runs while the market leaders disappoint. The handicap debutants prove better than their ratings suggest.

watchPoints.text: Minella Rockett returning after 176 days off may need this run badly despite previous promise at the trip
Fallacy has fading tendencies in the finish which could be exposed if the pace quickens significantly late
Watch how quickly Madbadanddangerous sets the early fractions as this will determine how the race unfolds
Johnny Soda's recent win came from well back so note his early positioning tactics under Adam Caffrey
Now Maybe faces a step up in class from maiden company to handicap level for the first time

runners_data.comment: Modest effort on debut when well behind Almazann, hard to see him turn that around

runners_data.name: Nosmokewithoutfire

runners_data.spotlight: 80-1 and tailed of on debut at Naas (7f, yld-sft); hard to fancy on that evidence.
